record.original_question: Is aabaacbaab 3-D0L-avoidable (i.e. is there a ternary morphism g such that g ω (a) avoids aabaacbaab)?

evidence.quote: Is aabaacbaab 3-D0L-avoidable (i.e. is there a ternary morphism g such that g ω (a) avoids aabaacbaab)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ (resp. $\Sigma^\omega$) denote the set of finite (resp. one-sided infinite) words over $\Sigma$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is a factor of a word $u$ (finite or infinite) if $u$ can be written as $u = x w y$ for some words $x, y$. 

A pattern over a set of variables $V$ is a non-empty word $p \in V^*$. An occurrence of $p$ in a word $u \in \Sigma^* \cup \Sigma^\omega$ is a non-erasing morphism $h \colon V^* \to \Sigma^*$ such that $h(p)$ is a factor of $u$. The word $u$ avoids $p$ if there is no occurrence of $p$ in $u$.

A morphism $g \colon \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ is prolongable on a letter $a \in \Sigma$ if $g(a) = a w$ for some non-empty word $w$ such that $g^n(w) \neq \varepsilon$ for all $n \geq 0$; in this case the iterates $g^n(a)$ form a sequence of prefixes converging to a unique infinite word $g^\omega(a) \in \Sigma^\omega$.

A pattern $p$ is said to be $k$-D0L-avoidable if there exist a $k$-letter alphabet $\Sigma$ (with $|\Sigma| = k$), a morphism $g \colon \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$, and a letter $a \in \Sigma$ such that $g$ is prolongable on $a$ and the infinite word $g^\omega(a)$ avoids $p$.

Question. Consider the alphabet $\Sigma = \{a, b, c\}$ (so $k = 3$), and view $aabaacbaab$ as a pattern over the variables $\{a, b, c\}$. Does there exist a morphism $g \colon \{a,b,c\}^* \to \{a,b,c\}^*$, prolongable on $a$, such that the infinite word $g^\omega(a)$ contains no factor of the form $h(aabaacbaab)$ for any non-erasing morphism $h$ — equivalently, such that $g^\omega(a)$ avoids the pattern $aabaacbaab$? In other words, is the pattern $aabaacbaab$ $3$-D0L-avoidable?
